heard: Four astronauts flew 252,756 miles from Earth to break a historic record. Launching in April 2026 aboard NASA's Space Launch System, Artemis II surpassed Apollo 13's deep space distance. Flying inside the Orion capsule integrity, the crew traveled on a lunar free-return trajectory without landing. ESA's European Service Module propelled the 10-day test flight to validate critical spacecraft systems. Commander Reed Weissman and pilot Victor Glover even completed manual proximity maneuvers using their rocket's upper stage. Mission specialists Christina Koch and Jeremy Hansen flew as the first woman and non-American beyond low Earth orbit since 1972. After a Pacific Ocean splashed down off San Diego, their flight proved how far people can venture into the cosmic unknown.
